blocks.content: A StorageClass defines a named category of storage, and how to actually provision it, enabling PVs to be created automatically on demand instead of always requiring an administrator to create them by hand.

A StorageClass is not storage itself, it is a template, naming a provisioner and its configuration (the exact type of cloud disk, its performance tier, and similar), describing how new storage of a given kind should be created.

blocks.alt: A named template describing how, not the storage itself

blocks.content:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-ssd
provisioner: kubernetes.io/aws-ebs
parameters:
  type: gp3

blocks.content: A cluster can define several StorageClasses side by side, a fast-ssd class for performance-sensitive workloads, a cheaper standard class for everything else, letting different applications request the storage tier that actually fits their needs.

blocks.alt: Different tiers, matched to what each workload actually needs

blocks.content: 3. Referenced by Name in a PVC
blocks.text: 3. Referenced by Name in a PVC

blocks.content: A PVC opts into a specific StorageClass with its storageClassName field, one more of the matching criteria covered in the previous topic, this is how a Pod's storage request ends up provisioned on the right kind of underlying storage.

blocks.alt: A PVC naming exactly which class of storage it wants

blocks.content:
spec:
  storageClassName: fast-ssd
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi

blocks.content: 4. The Mechanism Behind Automatic PV Creation
blocks.text: 4. The Mechanism Behind Automatic PV Creation

blocks.content: This is what makes dynamic provisioning, covered fully in the next topic, actually possible, a StorageClass's provisioner is the exact component that creates a brand new PV automatically, matching a PVC's request, with no administrator needing to pre-create anything.

blocks.alt: The mechanism enabling storage to be created on demand, covered next

blocks.content: Most clusters designate one StorageClass as the default, if a PVC does not specify storageClassName at all, it automatically uses that default class, this is why many PVC manifests in practice never mention a StorageClass explicitly.

blocks.alt: A sensible fallback, used automatically when nothing else is specified

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A StorageClass is a named template describing how to provision a category of storage, letting different workloads request different performance tiers by name.
It is the mechanism that makes dynamic, on-demand PV creation possible, and most clusters designate one class as the default for PVCs that do not specify one.
